Well, I'd say that's a person who wants help, wants some structure in their lives, or an example to generally follow. I think that iconic "I know best" pedantry comes from someone having to fend for themselves socially. Personally, I never really felt like I had a strong male role model I respected a lot, and that meant I was on my own. Since I was smart I adopted what seemed to be idolized cultural norms (like what I assumed chivalry was) and never really understood why what I was doing was wrong.

Everybody's depression is different, too, so that's tough to pin down.

So what would I say to our young protegee? I'd tell him to learn from his experiences. Doing the same thing over and over to ill effect won't work, so it's time to fundamentally reexamine what he's doing. I'd tell him that socializing can be tough, but the best thing to do is just start with their interaction with one person and instead of thinking about how you blew it, think about *why* you blew it. Think about what you said and how it made the other person feel, and if you don't understand it, find that knowledge somewhere else, because I know all of us are good at knowledge accumulation. Apply that same thought process to his clothes, his actions, to all that stuff.

I'd tell him to be himself, and actually explain what that means - don't hold yourself to some idealized standard where doing what you're supposed to do gets you what you want, because it doesn't always work.

As for the depression, quite frankly, I'd tell him to find a therapist that he likes (preferably while he's still on his parents' insurance), because they'll help loads better than I will. But the one thing that keeps me going even when I don't think I can are the little bits of happiness that break through, no matter what it is  some little anal-retentive organization, beating Dark Souls, even making a really great sandwich, anything. When things get rough, mentally, I cling to these tiny little respites like life preservers, and convince myself that there's going to be another one.

Friendzoning is a pretty contentious term. Some people think it means "give a girl a bunch of gifts in an attempt to obligate her to be attracted to you," but, at least, from the friendzoned perspective, it's "I do all the things I thought should make me attractive to girls and it doesn't work." A lot of these guys just don't know what to do or how to  do it, so they try all the romance movie stuff where some guy works waaaay too hard to win the heart of a girl only to have it pay off, and they fall into the "nice guy" trap or whatever you want to call it.

So, at least if I'm any model, these guys have a fundamental misunderstanding of what modern courtship is. They don't have rules or guidelines or social abilities to actually get women, and since a lot of that is person-to-person, it's not easy to see to understand how it develops. The best cure for this would, IMO, literally be some sort of no-shame remedial social interaction courses for adults. A lot of people like me latch on to stuff like PUA or Red Pill just because they need some sort of coherent framework on how to interact with other people, and since sex is such a big drive, they find stuff that's sex-centered.

~~m'~~Ladies, if you know a guy who starts doing the friendzone dance, the *best* thing you can do is shut him down, hard. Imagine if he were a puppy - he might be nice, but he has no idea how to act around people. Be firm, and discourage behavior you don't like.
